subject: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Sam / Alicia,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the candid conversation. Below is a quick recap to make sure we're aligned and to surface the next steps on our side. Please flag anything I missed.

Pain points you called out:
- Unit economics: current per-inference cost on your LLM endpoints is ~ $0.045/token equivalent for production traffic; this is unsustainable as usage scales.
- Latency requirements: 95th percentile should stay under ~200ms for customer-facing flows.
- Ops overhead: brittle autoscaling and heavy manual tuning when traffic spikes.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Model infra: Hugging Face-hosted models running on m5/GPU-backed EC2 via an internal inference service.
- Orchestration: homegrown autoscaler + CloudWatch alarms.
- Observability: basic Prometheus metrics and business metrics in Looker.

Success criteria for a pilot / evaluation
1) Reduce per-inference unit cost by >=50% while preserving quality.
2) Maintain p95 latency < 200ms for critical routes.
3) Prove stable autoscaling behavior under your traffic profile and demonstrate predictable cost.
4) Meet basic security requirements (SSO, audit logs) — SOC2 conversation to follow.

Technical constraints & openness
- Batching/caching: You�re open to batching and prefix/KV caching as long as we can keep latency guarantees for the critical path.
- Quantization: engineering is okay exploring 4-bit/8-bit quantization, but we need a short eval to validate no quality regressions on your core prompts.
- Fallbacks: prefer automatic fallback to a higher-cost model if a quantized variant shows drift.

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep dive (1hr) with your infra/ML engineer + our runtime lead to go over traffic shape, sequence lengths, and KV cache opportunities — target next week.
2) Pilot scope: 6-week pilot on a subset of routes (we outlined an approach in the attached redwood-quick-pilot-outline.pdf).
3) Pricing & SOW: I�ve attached a rough pricing-sheet and SOW-template; Ben (cc) will follow up on commercials.

Attach: redwood-quick-pilot-outline.pdf, pricing-sheet.xlsx

If this looks right, I can lock in a deep-dive time and loop in our runtime lead + solutions engineer.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures the convo. A few clarifications / asks from our side: 

- Cost: the $0.045/token equivalent was from our current averaging across multiple models; for the pilot we�d like to focus on the two highest-volume routes (customer-facing chat + fraud scoring) where cost matters most.
- Batching/caching: definitely open, but the chat route has low tolerance for added tail latency. If batching hurts p95 we�d need a hybrid approach (dedicated low-latency pool + batched cheaper pool).
- Quantization: engineering is willing to test 4-bit on one model if we can A/B quality against current floating-point baseline.
- Security: SOC2 + SSO are gating for procurement; we can share our security questionnaire after the deep dive.

One more thing: can you provide an example SLA for latency and an outline of rollback/fallback behavior if quantized models show drift? Our legal/procurement will ask.

Happy to go ahead with the technical deep dive next Tuesday or Wednesday afternoon PT.

Sam
